chunks: My father narrated to me, from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Abi Yahya al-Wasiti, from Abi al-Hasan al-Hadda', who said:
Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is a graveyard close to you which is called Buratha. One hundred and twenty thousand martyrs, like the martyrs of Badr, will be resurrected from it.

key_terms.بَرَاثَا: Buratha, a specific graveyard mentioned in the narration
key_terms.شُهَدَاءِ بَدْرٍ: Martyrs of Badr, referring to the companions who died in the Battle of Badr

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the graveyard Buratha mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the graveyard of Buratha, noting it will yield 120,000 martyrs comparable in status to those of the Battle of Badr. This narration underscores the Shia belief in the spiritual potency of specific burial sites and the concept of collective martyrdom, linking local sanctity to the foundational events of Islamic history.
